meta.title: Resizable Panel
meta.description: Split-pane layouts with smooth drag-to-resize, min/max constraints, and collapsible panels. Zero React re-renders during drag — CSS custom properties handle all position updates.

blocks.content: Split-pane layouts fail in the same ways every time. The handle fires dozens of state updates per drag, re-rendering the entire tree on every pixel. The panels jank. The rest of the UI flickers. You reach for a library that adds 40kb to solve a pointer-events problem.

ResizableRoot solves this at the architecture level. Panel sizes live as CSS custom properties — --panel-0, --panel-1 — written directly to the container element during drag. React never sees these updates. One re-render fires when you release the handle, committing the final sizes to state. The layout is always smooth.

blocks.title: How zero-rerender drag works
blocks.content: On pointerdown the handle calls setPointerCapture so events keep firing even when the cursor leaves. On pointermove it calls setSizeDirect(index, size) which writes containerEl.style.setProperty('--panel-N', size + '%') directly — bypassing React entirely. On pointerup, commitSizes() updates React state exactly once.
Drag the handles between panels. The left panel has a 12% minimum and 38% maximum. All three panels share the same 100% width.
No new npm dependencies. The system uses pointer events and CSS custom properties — nothing else.

steps.title: Add the files
steps.description: Copies the resizable folder into components/bevelui/.

blocks.content: Pass defaultSizes as an array of percentages summing to 100. The index prop on ResizablePanel and ResizableHandle maps each element to its size slot.
Add a panelConfigs array to set per-panel constraints. Index 0 here is collapsible with a 12% min and 38% max.

blocks.code:
<ResizableRoot
  defaultSizes={[20, 55, 25]}
  direction="horizontal"
  panelConfigs={[
    { minSize: 12, maxSize: 38, collapsible: true },
    { minSize: 30 },
    { minSize: 14, maxSize: 40 },
  ]}
  onResize={(sizes) => console.log(sizes)}
  className="h-screen"
>
  <ResizablePanel index={0}><FileTree /></ResizablePanel>
  <ResizableHandle index={0} />
  <ResizablePanel index={1}><Editor /></ResizablePanel>
  <ResizableHandle index={1} />
  <ResizablePanel index={2}><Inspector /></ResizablePanel>
</ResizableRoot>

blocks.content: Set direction to vertical for a top/bottom split. The handle becomes a horizontal bar and the size axis switches to height.

blocks.code:
<ResizableRoot
  defaultSizes={[60, 40]}
  direction="vertical"
  className="h-screen"
>
  <ResizablePanel index={0}><Canvas /></ResizablePanel>
  <ResizableHandle index={0} />
  <ResizablePanel index={1}><Console /></ResizablePanel>
</ResizableRoot>

blocks.title: Nesting splits
blocks.content: Nest a vertical ResizableRoot inside a horizontal one to get a full IDE-style layout — file tree on the left, editor top-right, terminal bottom-right. Each root manages its own CSS vars independently.
